narrativeReportMd:
# Composition R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Composition keeps its resource identity, but R6 contains multiple local hard instance-breaking content-model changes. The highest-impact R4-to-R6 breaks are removal of `confidentiality` and `section.mode`, and remodels of `attester.mode`, `relatesTo`, and `event`. R6 also creates major reverse-conversion risk through expanded required status codes, relaxed cardinalities, widened reference targets, and new optional metadata/participant/consent fields.

## Scope
This report is limited to local Composition changes in the supplied core packages. Inherited Element/Resource/DomainResource/datatype changes are listed as out of scope.

## Main migration themes
Migration requires structural transforms, terminology policy, and reverse-conversion policy. Primitive codes become CodeableConcepts, separate code/reference fields become CodeableReference, document-specific relationship targets broaden to general artifacts, and some R4 fields disappear.

## Highest-impact findings
See the findings for `Composition.confidentiality`, `Composition.attester.mode`, `Composition.relatesTo`, `Composition.event`, `Composition.section.mode`, and `Composition.status`.

## Follow-up analysis
Official narrative pages, terminology expansions, and ConceptMaps are needed before production migration decisions for security labels, relationship codes, event pairing, and status down-mapping.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: Composition has stable identity but material local breaking changes. Top concerns are removed/remodelled elements, status enum expansion, and R6 content that cannot round-trip to R4. Biggest uncertainty is official mapping/rationale for removed security/list-mode semantics and new relationship terminology.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Implement migration as a structural transform plus policy work: map primitive codes to CodeableConcepts, map event codes/references to CodeableReference, map relationship targets carefully, preserve removed confidentiality/section mode values, update status enums, and define lossy R6-to-R4 rules.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural deltas because both StructureDefinitions were present and compared. Confidence is medium for terminology equivalence and rationale because official diffs, narrative pages, expansions, and ConceptMaps were not supplied.

findings.title: Composition.confidentiality was removed

binding.description: Codes specifying the level of confidentiality of the composition.

semanticText.definition: The code specifying the level of confidentiality of the Composition.
semanticText.comment: R4 text says highly confidential documents must not be treated as if they are not.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 has no local Composition element at this path; any replacement must use another mechanism such as security labels or an extension.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances containing `confidentiality` have an element not present in R6. Because the field can drive privacy/access policy, silent loss is high business risk.

justification.inferredGoal: Move confidentiality handling to a broader security-label or policy mechanism.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep a deprecated 0..1 `confidentiality` field while directing new use to resource-level security labels.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of consolidating confidentiality into broader security labeling is reasonable, and security metadata is sensitive enough that duplicate canonical locations are risky. Removal is still a hard R4-to-R6 break for populated R4 instances, so the justification is only probable without official rationale or a required mapping.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have retained `Composition.confidentiality` as a deprecated optional element and specified how it relates to `meta.security`. That would preserve R4-valid payloads, but it would continue the R4 ambiguity between a single Composition-specific confidentiality code and general resource security labels. Conflicting values could affect access control, so this is only a partial alternative rather than a clean yes.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances but leaves two same-resource locations for security sensitivity, creating conflict and safety-governance burden.

evidence.detail: R4 defines 0..1 code with required v3 confidentiality binding.
Local terminology includes confidentiality classifications such as restricted and very restricted.

examples.examplesMd: Illustrative minimal R4 shape showing the removed field.

findings.narrativeMd: `Composition.confidentiality` disappeared from the local content model. Existing R4 documents with this element will fail strict R6 validation and require a deliberate security-metadata migration.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 `confidentiality` property is not allowed by R6 Composition. The finding is local to Composition, not an inherited Resource security-label change.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory populated values and map them to a governed target such as `meta.security` or an extension. Do not drop the value without security review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Removal might be justified if confidentiality belongs at Resource/security-label level, but a deprecated transition path or explicit ConceptMap would have been less disruptive.

findings.title: Composition.attester.mode changed from code to CodeableConcept

oldState.summary: Mandatory primitive code with required binding.

binding.description: The way in which a person authenticated a composition.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Local R4/R6 CodeSystems contain the same four codes.

binding.description: The way in which a person authenticated a composition.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Binding is weakened and representation is now CodeableConcept.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The JSON shape changes from a string to a CodeableConcept object. R6 CodeableConcepts with text, multiple codings, or local codes cannot be losslessly reduced to the single R4 code.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep primitive `attester.mode` and add an optional CodeableConcept sibling for richer attestation coding.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of allowing richer, potentially multi-system attestation-mode coding is reasonable. Because the old primitive code cannot express text, alternate systems, or multiple codings, preserving R4 shape while fully meeting the goal would require a parallel element and rules for which representation is authoritative.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A base R6 design could have retained `mode` as the R4 primitive code and introduced a new optional CodeableConcept element for richer coding. This would preserve existing R4 instances, but it would make implementations handle two fields for the same attestation fact and risk indefinite use of the deprecated primitive. That material duplication makes the alternative partial.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids the wire-format break but creates duplicate representations and leaves the primitive unable to carry full CodeableConcept semantics.

evidence.detail: R4 type is `code`; binding strength is required.
R6 type is `CodeableConcept`; binding strength is preferred.
Both local CodeSystems contain personal, professional, legal, official.

examples.examplesMd: Fragments focus on the changed mode shape.

findings.narrativeMd: The meaning is similar, but wire format and generated classes change. Existing R4 `attester.mode: "legal"` needs wrapping as a CodeableConcept coding.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid for any R4 attester with primitive mode. R6-to-R4 is lossy for text-only, multi-coding, or non-preferred concepts.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map R4 codes to CodeableConcept codings with system `http://hl7.org/fhir/composition-attestation-mode`; define reverse-selection policy.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: CodeableConcept is more extensible, but retaining the primitive or adding a transition choice would have reduced serializer breakage.

findings.title: Composition.relatesTo code/type and target choices were remodelled

oldState.summary: R4 used required primitive `code` plus target Identifier or Reference(Composition).

binding.description: The type of relationship between documents.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R4 local CodeSystem has replaces, transforms, signs, appends.

newState.summary: R6 uses required CodeableConcept `type` and target uri, Attachment, canonical(Resource), Reference(Resource), or markdown.

binding.description: The type of relationship to the related artifact.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The external R6 ValueSet was not found locally; StructureDefinition short text lists many relationship codes.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The relationship classifier moved from `code` to `type` and kept 1..1 cardinality, but changed type and binding.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 `relatesTo.code` and `targetIdentifier` are not valid R6 paths. R6 can target arbitrary artifacts/resources that R4 cannot represent.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent relationships to FHIR and non-FHIR artifacts.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `relatesTo.code` and `targetIdentifier` aliases while adding the broader R6 relationship type and target model.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Generalizing `relatesTo` from document-only relationships to relationships with FHIR and non-FHIR artifacts is a reasonable R6 goal. The less-breaking path would preserve old element names and target shapes, but it would leave multiple same-resource ways to express the relationship type and identifier target.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have kept `relatesTo.code` and `targetIdentifier` as deprecated fields and added `type` plus the broader target choices. That would cover most R4 instances, but it would require precedence and consistency rules across old and new classifier/target fields, including `targetIdentifier` versus `targetReference.identifier`. The duplicate representations and terminology ambiguity are material, so the alternative is partial.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old payloads but duplicates classifier and identifier representations, with ambiguous mapping between old document relationships and broad artifact relationships.

evidence.detail: R4 classifier is required code bound to document-relationship-type.
R4 target choices are Identifier or Reference(Composition).
R6 classifier is CodeableConcept with extensible artifact-relationship-type binding.
R6 target choices are uri, Attachment, canonical(Resource), Reference(Resource), and markdown.

examples.examplesMd: R6 comment recommends targetReference.identifier when only an identifier is available.

findings.narrativeMd: `relatesTo` is a structural remodel: the classifier name/type changed and the target choice domain broadened substantially.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid for `relatesTo.code` and `targetIdentifier`. R6-to-R4 is lossy for non-Composition references and non-reference target choices.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map old codes into `relatesTo.type` after terminology review. Map targetIdentifier to targetReference.identifier. Reject or extension-preserve R6 uri/Attachment/canonical/markdown targets when converting to R4.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Generalization is useful, but deprecated aliases or a standard mapping would have made the change less breaking.

findings.title: Composition.event.code/detail merged into CodeableReference detail

oldState.summary: R4 separated event.code CodeableConcept 0..* and event.detail Reference(Resource) 0..*.

newState.summary: R6 removes event.code and changes event.detail to CodeableReference(Resource) 0..*.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: R6 detail definition says events may be included as a code or a reference.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 event codes are at a removed path and R4 detail references need wrapping as CodeableReference.reference. R6 CodeableReference pairs may lose semantics if split back to R4 arrays.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep R4 `event.code` and Reference-valued `event.detail` while adding a new optional CodeableReference field.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Using CodeableReference for events is a coherent way to model code, reference, or both. The breaking design also avoids maintaining sibling R4 arrays plus a new normalized representation, which would be hard to keep consistent.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have kept `event.code` and the old Reference form of `event.detail`, then added a new CodeableReference element for systems that need paired code/reference semantics. This would preserve old payloads but would duplicate the event fact and require rules for whether old arrays or the new CodeableReference are authoritative. Because the old model also has pairing ambiguity, this is only a partial alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances but creates parallel event representations and ambiguity about pairing concepts with references.

evidence.detail: R4 event.code is CodeableConcept with ActCode example binding.
R6 event.detail is CodeableReference(Resource) with ActCode example binding.

examples.examplesMd: Pairing decisions may require domain review.

findings.narrativeMd: Event representation changed from sibling code/reference arrays to a single CodeableReference array.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid for `event.code` and for bare Reference objects at `event.detail`. R6-to-R4 may be lossy when a CodeableReference has both concept and reference.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Transform R4 codes to `detail.concept` and R4 references to `detail.reference`. Decide whether code/reference values should be paired or separate.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 model is cleaner, but a dual-path transition would have reduced migration ambiguity.

findings.title: Composition.section.mode was removed

oldState.summary: R4 optional 0..1 section processing mode code.

binding.description: The processing mode that applies to this section.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R4 codes are working, snapshot, changes.

semanticText.comment: R4 says a change list must not be misunderstood as a complete list.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 has no local field for section list processing mode.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 sections with `mode` fail R6 validation and may lose safety-relevant list-completeness semantics.

justification.inferredGoal: Simplify Composition section content or move list semantics elsewhere.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain optional `section.mode` as deprecated with clearer guidance or warnings against unsafe use.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The local definitions show a safety-relevant R4 element and no direct R6 replacement. Because `section.mode` was already optional and could have been retained with deprecation text, the same simplification goal could likely have been met without invalidating R4 instances that carry working/snapshot/changes semantics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A base R6 design could have kept `Composition.section.mode` at 0..1 with its existing codes, marked it deprecated or discouraged, and clarified that profiles should define when it is meaningful. That preserves R4 instances and the important warning that a change list must not be read as complete. The tradeoff is carrying a legacy field, but the long-term burden appears low to moderate because there is no competing R6 base element for this fact.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeps a legacy list-mode field, but avoids data loss and does not duplicate a new R6 base field for the same fact.

evidence.detail: R4 defines 0..1 code with required list-mode binding.
R4 warns that change lists must not be mistaken for complete lists.

examples.examplesMd: The `changes` code is the riskiest semantic case.

findings.narrativeMd: `section.mode` removal is a hard shape break and can remove whether a section is a working list, snapshot, or changes-only list.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Any R4 section with `mode` is old-valid/new-invalid. R6 has no direct local replacement path.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Preserve populated values in a governed extension, section note, or profile-specific rule; do not silently drop `changes` semantics.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A deprecation period or extension would have been less disruptive, especially because R4 text identifies interpretation risk.

findings.title: Composition.status required value set expanded

oldState.summary: R4 required status codes: preliminary, final, amended, entered-in-error.

newState.summary: R6 required status adds registered, partial, corrected, appended, cancelled, deprecated, unknown.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R4 codes remain; R6 adds lifecycle states.

impact.impactRationaleMd: No R4 code was removed, but R6 adds required-binding values that closed R4 enums, validators, and workflows cannot represent.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent more precise Composition workflow lifecycle.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: R4 status codes remain valid in R6, so this is not an old-valid/new-invalid base-design break.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The added status codes provide more precise workflow lifecycle states and do not remove any R4 status. They can break reverse conversion and exhaustive enum consumers, but that is not a backward-compatible alternative question for preserving R4-valid instances in base R6.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed for R4-to-R6 instance validity because the R4 code set is retained. ConceptMaps, enum updates, or down-conversion policies are important mitigations for R6-to-R4 and runtime compatibility, but they are not base-design alternatives under this calibration.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is R6-to-R4 down-mapping and closed-enum runtime handling for new lifecycle states, not preservation of R4 instances.

evidence.detail: R4 short text lists four required codes.
R6 short text lists eleven required codes.
Local R6 CodeSystem adds registered, partial, corrected, appended, cancelled, deprecated, unknown.

examples.examplesMd: `registered` is a valid R6 status but not an R4 status.

findings.narrativeMd: `Composition.status` remains required and modifier, but its allowed code set expanded substantially.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 is not hard-breaking for known R4 codes. R6-to-R4 is high risk because new statuses are invalid R4 and may break exhaustive enum switches.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update enums and workflow logic. Define explicit down-maps such as corrected/appended to amended and partial to preliminary only if clinically acceptable.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Finer states are useful, but adding required-binding codes is not compatible with closed R4 clients without a ConceptMap.

findings.title: R6 relaxes required/singular Composition cardinalities

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 required author and title and allowed only one identifier and subject.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 permits missing author/title and multiple identifiers/subjects.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Looser R6 cardinalities create valid R6 instances that are invalid R4 and change nullability/list assumptions in generated code.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: the R6 cardinality changes relax minima or widen maxima and preserve R4-valid instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing missing author/title and multiple identifiers/subjects broadens valid R6 content, but it does not make valid R4 Composition instances invalid in R6. The compatibility concern is R6-to-R4 representability and generated-code assumptions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because these are permissive base changes, `backwardCompatibleAlternativeAvailable` is not applicable. Keeping R4 cardinalities would improve R6-to-R4 round-tripping, but it would also block the stated R6 broadening rather than serve as a less-breaking way to preserve R4 instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The cost is reverse-conversion policy and updated nullability/list assumptions, not an R4-to-R6 validation break.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment omits R4-required author/title and repeats subject.

findings.narrativeMd: These are permissive for forward validation but important for reverse conversion and runtime assumptions.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4 instance becomes invalid because a min decreased or max increased. R6 instances without author/title or with repeated identifier/subject do not validate as R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Treat author/title as optional and identifier/subject as arrays in R6 models. For R6-to-R4, require policy for synthesizing, choosing, rejecting, or extension-preserving values.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Profiles could have relaxed these constraints less disruptively, but base relaxation may reflect broader intended use.

findings.title: Several reference target domains widened

oldState.summary: R4 excludes CareTeam author/section.author, Group attester, and Patient/Group custodian. Custodian is Organization only.

newState.summary: R6 adds CareTeam to author and section.author, Group to attester.party, and Patient/Group to custodian.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 references remain valid in R6, but new R6 target types are invalid in R4 and may break target-type switches.

justification.inferredGoal: Permit team, group, and patient actors in Composition metadata.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: adding reference targets widens R6 and keeps R4 target choices valid.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Permitting CareTeam, Group, and Patient actors appears to support real-world author, attester, and custodian roles. Since R4 targets were not removed, this is not an old-valid/new-invalid base-design break.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible alternative is applicable for R4-to-R6 preservation because target-domain widening is already backward-compatible for existing R4 references. Extensions or proxy mappings may help when converting new R6 targets back to R4, but those are reverse-conversion mitigations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: New R6 targets complicate R6-to-R4 conversion and business-rule switches, but do not require a less-breaking R6 base alternative.

evidence.detail: R6 custodian targets Organization, Patient, Group.

examples.examplesMd: Shown targets are valid under R6 widened domains, not R4.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 broadens who can author, attest, or maintain a Composition.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R6 references to CareTeam, Group, or Patient custodians do not validate in R4 for these fields.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update validators and authorization logic. Reverse conversion needs proxy mapping, extension preservation, or rejection.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Widening targetProfiles is standard, but extensions would have been more R4-compatible.

findings.title: R6 adds optional metadata, consent, request, participant, and note elements

affectedLocation.newPath: Composition.url / version / useContext / consent / basedOn / participant / name / note / section.note

oldState.summary: R4 has no local base elements at these paths.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 lacks first-class slots for these concepts.

newState.summary: R6 adds url, version, useContext, consent, basedOn, participant, name, note, and section.note.
newState.narrativeMd: All are optional, but can carry important metadata/provenance/consent/annotation content.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Optional additions do not break old R4 instances, but populated R6 fields have no R4 base location and may be rejected by strict R4 clients or lost in conversion.

justification.inferredGoal: Add canonical identity, use context, consent, request, participants, and notes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: optional additive R6 elements are already a backward-compatible base-design pattern for R4-to-R6.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding optional first-class slots for canonical identity, context, consent, request linkage, participants, names, and notes is a normal compatible evolution of the base resource. The change creates reverse-conversion work but no R4-to-R6 invalidation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backward-compatible alternative is not applicable because the base design is already additive and optional. R4 extensions can support round-trip mitigation for populated R6-only fields, but extensions are not a less-breaking R6 base design in this case.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Populated R6-only elements need R4 extension or data-loss policy, but absent elements do not affect R4-valid instances.

examples.examplesMd: All shown fields are R6-only base elements.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 optional additions are not forward-breaking but create reverse-conversion data-loss risk.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 is safe when these are absent. R6-to-R4 requires extensions or data loss for populated new elements.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define R4 extension mappings, especially for consent, basedOn, participant, and notes. Test strict R4 clients against R6 payloads.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Optional base elements are a reasonable evolution path; extensions would be more R4-compatible but less native to R6.

findings.title: Composition.category example binding changed

oldState.summary: Example binding to document-classcodes; R4 comment references XDS/MHD metadata.

binding.description: High-level kind of a clinical document at a macro level.

newState.summary: Example binding to referenced-item-category; XDS/MHD comment removed.

binding.description: High-level kind of a clinical document at a macro level.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Example bindings do not reject codes, but picklists/profiles generated from the base binding may change.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: the element shape is unchanged and the binding remains example strength, so base R4 instances are not invalidated.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Retargeting the example binding to a referenced-item category value set is plausibly reasonable, and example bindings do not constrain instance validity. Confidence remains limited for terminology equivalence without expansion comparison, but the level of base breakage is low.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Keeping the old example binding would have been a continuity choice, but it is not a backward-compatible alternative in the calibrated sense because the R6 base change does not make R4 category codings invalid. Implementers should compare profile bindings and expansions rather than treat this as an R4-to-R6 base break.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Generated picklists or profile assumptions may drift, but this is terminology guidance rather than a base validation break.

evidence.detail: R4 described this as XDS/MHD metadata.

examples.examplesMd: No compact JSON example included; see narrative for mechanism.

findings.narrativeMd: The element shape is unchanged, but terminology guidance shifted away from the R4 document-classcodes example.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Base validation should not fail because the binding is example strength. The risk is semantic/profile/tooling drift.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not rewrite category codings solely due to this base example binding. Compare profile bindings and expansions before changing picklists.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This is low-disruption but could have preserved the old example binding for continuity.

findings.title: R6 adds warning constraint cmp-3 for attested Composition content

oldState.summary: R4 section constraints include cmp-1 and cmp-2, not cmp-3.

newState.summary: R6 adds cmp-3 warning: if attester exists then Composition needs text or section.

constraints.human: If attester exists then the Composition either needs a text or a section

impact.impactRationaleMd: Warning severity should not make instances invalid, but pipelines that fail on warnings may be affected.

justification.inferredGoal: Encourage attested Compositions to include text or sections.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: the added constraint is warning severity and does not make R4 instances invalid in base R6.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Encouraging attested Compositions to contain text or sections is reasonable, and using warning severity is already a compatibility-conscious design. This is not a hard R4-to-R6 base validation break.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base alternative is needed for instance validity. Narrative-only guidance would be softer, but the warning constraint preserves base validity while making the quality expectation computable.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Warning-as-error local pipelines may need policy updates, but the base specification chose a low-breaking warning rather than an error.

examples.examplesMd: An attested metadata-only Composition may warn in R6; no hard-invalid example is provided because severity is warning.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a quality warning tying attestation to actual text or section content.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not hard old-valid/new-invalid because severity is warning, but warning-as-error validation pipelines can be disrupted.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Check validator policy. Add text/sections to attested Compositions or document why warnings are acceptable.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A warning is already a less-breaking alternative to an error invariant.
